sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Des Plaines, IL?
sections.html:
An owner in Des Plaines can hire a broker, go it alone, or take cash from a purchaser who buys the house as it is. Repair needs, tenants in the unit and a firm closing date tend to decide which path fits.

  • A full listing can fetch strong prices where the middle home value is $335,600, but it brings showings, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • Selling alone skips the commission and makes the contract and disclosures your job.
  • A cash deal shortens the calendar and suits estates, rentals and houses with postponed maintenance.

Because Des Plaines sits beside O'Hare and two tollways, buyers range from commuters to investors who want rentals near the airport and the Metra line.

sections.h2: What makes Des Plaines distinct for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Des Plaines is a Cook County city that sits just north of O'Hare International Airport and takes its name from the river that runs along its east side. Its 14 square miles held 60,675 people in 2020.

French explorers named the river for the sycamores they thought resembled European plane trees. American settlers arrived after the 1833 Treaty of Chicago, followed by German immigrants. The Chicago, St. Paul and Fond du Lac Railroad built through in 1857, the stop took the Des Plaines name in 1859, and voters converted the village to a city in 1925. Postwar growth took off with O'Hare next door, lifting the census count from 14,994 in 1950 to 57,239 in 1970.

The road network includes Interstates 90 and 294, U.S. 12, 14 and 45, and Illinois 58, 72 and 83. Commuters board Union Pacific Northwest Line trains at the Des Plaines and Cumberland stations, and the Pace Pulse Dempster Line links Evanston with O'Hare. The city's 2021 annual financial report names these major employers: Rivers Casino, Universal Oil Products, Oakton College, Sysco, Juno Lighting, Holy Family Medical Center, Wheels Inc. and LSG Sky Chefs.

Younger students go to District 62, 59 or 63 schools, and high schoolers go to Maine West in District 207.

sections.h2: What does the census say about Des Plaines housing costs?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 58,772 residents for mid-2025, 3.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base of 60,653. Owners live in most homes, and 34.2 percent of residents were born outside the United States.

Because 92.3 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, few houses change hands, which leaves sellers with fewer recent nearby sales as price guides.

sections.h2: What local details come up with Des Plaines buyers?
sections.html:
The city uses ZIP codes 60016 through 60019 and area codes 847 and 224, at an elevation of 642 feet. Rivers Casino opened in July 2011 on roughly 21 acres next to the Tri-State Tollway at Devon Avenue and Des Plaines River Road, after the Illinois Gaming Board awarded the state's tenth casino license in 2008. It appears among the city's major employers.

Under parts of town lies the Des Plaines Disturbance, a zone of badly fractured rock that may mark an ancient meteorite crater 75 to 200 feet down, filled long ago by glacial activity. Nothing shows on the surface, and it rarely matters to a sale, but local lore makes it a conversation point.

Oakton College keeps a campus in the city, and Holy Family Medical Center also appears on the employer list.

sections.h2: Does a river, tornado history or flooding matter when selling a Des Plaines house?
sections.html:
Yes. A buyer or lender will ask about flooding. The McDonald's museum in town was torn down in 2018 after repeated flooding, and the river runs just east of downtown. Disclose any basement water or insurance claims and keep your repair receipts.

The earliest known Illinois tornado struck the site of modern Des Plaines on May 22, 1855, and spring storms here can still turn severe. The O'Hare station nearby averages 38.4 inches of snowfall, which is hard on roofs and gutters.

One more local quirk affects sellers: addresses inside city limits use the Des Plaines numbering system, while unincorporated parts of Maine Township with a Des Plaines mailing address follow Chicago's grid. Confirm with the city whether your parcel is incorporated, since that decides which city rules and which transfer tax apply.

sections.h2: How do Cook County recording and transfer taxes affect a Des Plaines sale?
sections.html:
A Des Plaines deed is recorded by the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. The clerk's schedule prices a deed at $107, a total that folds in the GIS, document storage and rental housing support fees, plus $5 per document for mail-back recording.

Three layers of transfer tax can apply, and the Clerk's list names the seller as the party liable on each:

  • State of Illinois: .50 per $500.00 of value, matching the rate in 35 ILCS 200/31-10.
  • Cook County: .25 per $500.00.
  • City of Des Plaines: 2.00 per $1,000.00, evidenced by a rubber stamp, with a $10.00 fee for exempt transfers.

The Clerk calls its municipal list a courtesy that is not legally binding, so phone the city's listed number, 847-391-5325, to confirm the stamp before closing.

sections.h2: How are Des Plaines property taxes billed and appealed?
sections.html:
Cook County splits the year's tax into two bills. Per the Treasurer's primer, the first equals 55 percent of last year's total and is typically due March 1, while homeowner and senior exemptions show up on the second. Interest on late payments runs 1.5 percent monthly.

Values come from the Cook County Assessor. Maine Township, which covers parts of Des Plaines, received new values on June 4, 2025, the latest turn in a three-year cycle. In 2026 the north suburbs are reassessed only where something changed, such as a permit. Maine's 2026 appeal window at the Assessor shut on July 21, and the Board of Review accepted appeals from August 31 through September 29, 2026.

Have the PIN ready when you talk to the Treasurer or Assessor, because Cook County identifies every parcel by a 14-digit number. Your closing agent will explain how the year's bill is divided at the table.

sections.h2: Which Des Plaines rules cover rentals and repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
Rental owners in Des Plaines need a rental license, and an ordinance passed on February 2, 2009 makes them complete Phase 1 of the Crime Free Multi-Housing Program. A first-time license applicant must attend the seminar beforehand.

Repair permits are filed online through the city's self-service portal, and express guides exist for sheds, decks, fences, driveways, roofs and non-structural kitchen or bath remodels. The city adopted the 2021 I-Codes, effective January 1, 2026, and its permit page lists construction hours of 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday. Inspections of rental dwellings or permitted work are booked at 847-391-5382 or permits@desplainesil.gov.

Closing out open permits before listing keeps unfinished work from surfacing late in a sale. Construction work in the city also needs a registered contractor, and contractor registration now runs through the same online portal, so a seller hiring out repairs should confirm the contractor is registered before the work starts.

If you plan to sell a rental, the city's rental dwelling inspection line is a useful first call, since it lets you learn what an inspector would flag before a buyer's inspector does.

faqs.q: Who is liable for transfer tax on a Des Plaines sale?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk's list shows the seller as liable for the state, county and city taxes. Your contract can allocate it differently, so confirm with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Where is a Des Plaines deed filed?
faqs.a: With the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. Title companies can also submit deeds electronically.

faqs.q: Is a license needed to lease my Des Plaines house?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental property owners must obtain a license and complete the Crime Free Multi-Housing seminar before a new license is issued.

faqs.q: Does a Des Plaines mailing address mean I am in the city?
faqs.a: Not always. Some unincorporated Maine Township addresses carry a Des Plaines mailing address but follow Chicago's numbering. Ask the city to confirm that your parcel is within the limits.

faqs.q: Is the Maine Township appeal window still open?
faqs.a: The 2026 filing windows with the Assessor and the Board of Review have closed. Cook County sets new windows by township each year, so check the Assessor's assessment calendar for the next opening.
